name: Cnoc Meadha
text: Cnoc Meadha is a hill west of Tuam in Co. Galway. Maps spell the name Knockmagha, Knockma, or Knock Ma. Tradition seats Finnbheara there, the king who rules the fairy host of Connacht. Two large cairns crown the hill. One cairn is held to cover Finnbheara. The other is held to cover Queen Medb. Some say her name survives inside the name Cnoc Meadha. The hill joins the fairy king and the great queen in one place.

attributes.attribute: the Galway hill of the fairy king Finnbheara
carries cairns said to bury Finnbheara and Queen Medb

okr.objective: Cnoc Meadha is the Galway hill where the fairy king Finnbheara and Queen Medb are said to lie.
key_results: Also written Mheadha, and appearing on maps as Knockmagha or Knockma.
West of Tuam, and called Castlehacket in English usage.
Holds two cairns tied to Finnbheara and to Queen Medb.
